attributes.law_screen: attempt.damage-enemy-constant-lifetime-closure.20260829.v1 concludes 'do not retry these branch axes WITHOUT new compiler evidence or a surrounding structural change'. The evidence condition was met: claim.law.guard-polarity-restructure-fixes-count-parity-not-form.20260831.v1 is newer than the cap and prescribes exactly this situation - an object one branch instruction short of target, with the residual already diagnosed as register-coloring-driven. APPLIED, and it paid. claim.law.if-else-arm-swap-controls-fallthrough-placement.20260831.v1 SCREENED and NOT applicable: its own recorded boundary is this very site (it cites `damage == 0 ? 2 : 3` vs the inverted spelling compiling byte-identically), and the arms here are not a scalar ternary. claim.law.fuzzy-can-underweight-a-real-improvement SCREENED against its counter-case attempt.enemy-extern-literal-sweep.20260831.v1, which found the law INVERTED in this same function - so the metric conflict was resolved by reading the aligned disassembly, not by preferring either metric a priori (see residual). Peephole route SCREENED and NOT retried: attempt.enemy-c-deepscrutiny.20260830.v1 records that a scoped `#pragma peephole off` cannot be undone (`#pragma reset` does not restore it), poisoned downstream functions and tripped WebFrank's hash guard - and ~10 functions including 2 pinned ones follow damage_enemy in source order.
attributes.residual: IMPROVED: fndiff real 151 -> 66 and instruction count went from 570/571 (off by one) to EXACT 571/571, by replacing two `if (...) goto store_fight;` guards plus the `store_fight:` label with one goto-free `if (e->health <= upper && e->type != E_DEATH) { ... }`. METRIC CONFLICT, resolved by reading the diff: objdiff fuzzy DIPPED 99.4046% -> 99.2207% while real improved 151 -> 66. The aligned fnasm --diff shows fuzzy is wrong here and real is right. Before, the whole function past 0x5b0 was displaced 4 bytes and EVERY downstream branch carried a wrong displacement (rendering as opcode-only `~` matches). After, addresses realign and downstream instructions including their branch targets (`ble ->5c8` @5b8, `b ->5d0` @5c4, `bne ->610` @5dc) become EXACT matches. The trade is local: at 0x5a4 we now emit `cror eq,lt,eq` + `bne` where target has a single `bgt`, losing one previously-matching instruction, in exchange for correct branch displacements across the remaining ~180 instructions. That is unambiguously closer to byte-exact, so the change is kept. REMAINING residual is two clusters: T@5a4 ['bgt'] vs ours ['cror','bne'], and T@5ac ['bne','b'] vs ours ['beq'] - the target folds its first guard to one branch but leaves the second as an UNFOLDED `bne`-to-the-next-instruction plus `b`, a goto-pair shape that this project's notes associate with peephole being off at that site. Plus the known whole-function FPR/GPR rotation (f3<->f1, f5<->f6, r5<->r7). DO-NOT-RETRY, each measured this session: (1) empty-true-block `if (t != E_DEATH) {} else goto store_fight;` - NEUTRAL, MWCC folds it to the same beq, a fourth folding form after the cap's structured-condition / explicit-if-else-label / one-case-switch-goto trio; (2) splitting the retained `&&` into two nested ifs - byte-IDENTICAL output, MWCC re-merges through the same cror, so per the two-identical-A/Bs rule that sub-axis is dead; (3) keeping guard 1 as a goto (which does restore the target's matching `bgt`) with guard 2 nested - REGRESSED straight back to 570/151, i.e. the matching bgt and the instruction-count parity are mutually exclusive under every form tried, and parity is worth far more. PARTIAL OVERTURN NOTICE for the integrator: attempt.damage-enemy-constant-lifetime-closure.20260829.v1's blanket 'do not retry branch axes' conclusion is now superseded in substance - the guard-polarity axis was productive - but its constant-lifetime findings and its fight-web cap still stand and should be preserved when that record is next revised.
